subject: Exec brief: burst SLAs, batching & KV-cache impacts for QBR prep
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-03-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exec brief: burst SLAs, batching & KV-cache impacts for QBR prep

Team — attaching the short brief for tomorrow's QBR dry run (attachments: burst_modeling_v2.xlsx, runway_calcs.pdf). High-level summary up front and two asks at the bottom.

TL;DR:
- Immediate decision: commit a small burst pool for the next quarter to cover marketing/product campaigns that peak at 2–3x baseline. Options below (A/B/C).
- Primary levers: reserved burst slots, per-route batching windows, and KV-prefix caching aggressiveness.
- Current numbers (baseline week of 3/20–3/26):
  • GPU spend run-rate: ~$1.02M/mo (hosted inference + Dedicated bursts)
  • Average GPU utilization across pools: 62%
  • KV cache global hit rate (chat-heavy routes): 28% (varies by customer)
  • Estimated marginal token cost saved by better batching/prefix caching: 15–30% depending on route mix

Scenario impact (quick):
- Option A (conservative): add 120 burst slots (NVIDIA A100 equiv), cost +$95k/mo, runway +11 days under 3x peak; KV/caching improvements deferred to next sprint.
- Option B (balanced): add 240 burst slots, enable route-level batching window increases (default +15ms), and aggressive KV-prefix caching for chat routes; cost +$180k/mo, effective token-cost reduction ~17% (net). Runway +22 days under 3x peak.
- Option C (aggressive): add 360 burst slots + proactive auto-fallback policies to quantized variants under load; cost +$255k/mo, token-cost reduction ~25%, but p95 latency risk for <200-token requests increases unless we route by SLA.

Notes on risks and trade-offs:
- Increasing batching windows improves amortized GPU utilization but raises p95 for short interactive calls. We quantify this in the attached modeling.
- KV-prefix caching yield is highest for chat-heavy customers; onboarding needs per-customer prompt-set evaluation to avoid hallucination drift.
- SLA exposure: we should pair any burst commit with a rollback/fallback policy to prevent latency SLO violations in low-latency routes.

Asks (need answers by EOD Tue 3/28):
1) Leadership decision: pick A/B/C (or a hybrid — propose %) so we can finalize procurement commit sizes.
2) Approve pilot rollout: route-level batching changes for up to 20% of traffic and enable KV-prefix caching for two flagship customers as a safety test.

Action items in attachments. I left a one‑page summary for the Exec QBR slide deck under the Drive link.

— Mina Haddad
Director, Infra Economics
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Exec brief: burst SLAs, batching & KV-cache impacts for QBR prep

Thanks Mina — clear summary. I lean toward Option B as the default for the QBR ask (balanced cost / runway).
Two quick asks before I sign off:
- Please include a 1‑line runway sensitivity for a 4x instead of 3x peak (just to see downside tails).
- In the Exec slide, call out the user impact for p95 increases explicitly (we need a single line for that).

If those two items are good we can greenlight B during the dry run.

— Lauren
VP, Product Ops
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-27T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec brief: burst SLAs, batching & KV-cache impacts for QBR prep

Agree with Lauren on B. A couple of operational guardrails I want in writing before commit:
- Auto-fallback policy: when load on a pool >85% for >3min, traffic should shift to cheaper quantized model variant and to a lower-cost region if latency still holds. This avoids SLA breaches.
- Canary percentage: rollout batching window changes to 5% traffic, measure p50/p95 for 24h, then 20% for 48h before wider release.

Also: estimate downstream revenue impact if we throttle high-cost customers during peak? If we lose a single high-volume campaign, cost savings might not be worth churn risk. I think the modeling should include 1 worst-case churned account with ARR impact.

— Dylan
Head of Reliability
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-27T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec brief: burst SLAs, batching & KV-cache impacts for QBR prep

Technical addendum (short):
- Batching trade-offs:
  • Increasing batch window from 5ms -> 20ms yields ~12% throughput improvement on transformer feed-forward kernels for 1k token avg sequences, but adds ~30–45ms p95 for 40–120 token requests.
  • CPU scheduling: larger batch windows increase CPU spike variance; we should cap batching per-core to avoid noisy neighbors.
- KV-prefix caching:
  • Measured hit-rate uplift for aggressive prefix caching in internal tests: +18–33% depending on prompt entropy. For chat flows where context re-use is high (session lengths >6 turns), hit-rates exceed 40%.
  • Consistency: must include TTL-based invalidation and a re-eval for any safety-sensitive prompts before enabling customer-wide.
- Implementation plan: per-route config (boolean + window_ms + fallback_model_id) with feature-flag rollout. Estimated infra work 3 engineers x 3 sprints + QA.

I'll attach a short CSV with sample hit rates (kvcache-hitrate-sample.csv) and a condensed config diff for the runtime.

— Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Exec brief: burst SLAs, batching & KV-cache impacts for QBR prep — decision & next steps

Thanks all — consolidating decisions below so the QBR slide is final.
Decisions (approved):
- Option B adopted as the baseline quarter ask: +240 burst slots, route-level batching window bump (default +15ms) and targeted KV-prefix caching for two flagship customers.
- Canary & rollback: follow Dylan's canary cadence (5% -> 20% -> wider) and auto-fallback at >85% pool load.
- Runway sensitivity: attached runway_calcs.pdf updated to include 4x tail scenario (see sheet 'tails').

Action items and owners:
- Procurement: finalize 240-slot burst purchase and term (procurement@bytecloud.com) — owner: procurement@bytecloud.com — due 4/6.
- Runtime: implement per-route config + feature flag for batching & fallback — owner: karthik_iyer — due 4/20 (eng effort note: 3 eng x 3 sprints).
- Product/Ops: define two pilot customers and safety eval checklist for KV-prefix caching — owner: lauren_bishop — due 4/3.
- Finance: incorporate +$180k/mo into next month forecast and update runway modeling with a 1-account churn sensitivity — owner: finance (cc'd externally).

I'll push the final one-pager to the Drive link and add a single-line call-out on p95 user impact for the exec slide as requested. If no objections I will finalize the QBR deck by EOD Friday.

Attachments referenced above: burst_modeling_v2.xlsx; runway_calcs.pdf; kvcache-hitrate-sample.csv

— Mina Haddad
Director, Infra Economics
